_comment: The Attack Surface Reduction rules NRG requires and the mode each must be in. Approved 2026-10-02 (Microsoft's three standard protection rules, Block) and widened by the owner 2026-10-25 to the 17 rules of the CIS Microsoft Intune for Microsoft Defender Antivirus Benchmark v1.0.0, Level 1 - Workstation (recommendations 2.10 to 2.26), each with the mode the benchmark requires: Block, or 'Audit or higher' (Audit, Warn or Block) where the benchmark accepts audit (rules that can break legitimate software, such as PSExec and WMI process creation beside Configuration Manager). Id is matched as a substring of the rule key the Settings Catalog reports (the setting definition id after 'attacksurfacereductionrules_'): the three original ids were seen in a real tenant read; the fourteen added are distinctive fragments of the rule name, because Microsoft publishes no Graph sample of the ASR keys, and docs/TP-LIVE-VALIDATION.md asks the first live run to confirm each one matches. A fragment that matches nothing reports the rule as NotConfigured, a false shortfall, never a false pass. Accept lists the modes that meet the requirement; an entry without Accept requires Block. An EMPTY list means no standard is approved and INT-2.2 leaves the rule-set half not assessed.
